title: AES-256: RAM-input xtime: one byte, N16 (Blömer–Seifert, FC2003)

target.description: One byte of the initial128-bit AES-256 master-key portion, using RAM-input xtime and the source's expected N≈16 selected input values.

setting.key_relation: One fixed secret master key; no related-key oracle.
setting.key_population: Arbitrary key of the stated AES instance in an implementation meeting the fault and feedback assumptions.
setting.plaintext_model: For a target first-round key byte, use chosen values i=0,...,N-1 in its plaintext byte; other bytes are arbitrary/random. Whole-key extension repeats for the required key material, with adaptive inputs for long keys.

fault_model.target: The most significant bit of the writable input-state byte before lookup in an immutable256-byte xtime ROM table.
fault_model.granularity: One selected input-state bit in RAM; the ROM table itself is not corrupted.
fault_model.timing: After first-round ShiftRows and before the target xtime lookup.
fault_model.location: The RAM input-bit location used for the target byte's xtime lookup.
fault_model.value_control: Force the input byte's MSB to zero; an existing zero is unchanged.
fault_model.sample_pairing: Each attempted injection yields a correct/incorrect outcome. Ciphertext-comparison feedback additionally needs a correct reference for the same input, outside the stated attempt count.
fault_model.feedback: Observable correct-versus-incorrect encryption outcome. Section1 permits alternatives: a device reset/error flag; comparison with a fault-free ciphertext; or detectable recomputation timing. Only the binary outcome is required, not the faulty ciphertext bytes. An unchanged correct output means the reset input bit was0; an incorrect output means it was1.

assumptions: Successful localization and the stipulated fault-value effect are model assumptions, not measured acquisition success rates.
The ciphertext-validity alternatives are interchangeable only as a binary observation; the source does not cost each feedback channel's calibration or reference executions separately.
Recovery target: One byte of the initial128-bit AES-256 master-key portion, using RAM-input xtime and the source's expected N≈16 selected input values.

The implementation must expose precisely the specified temporary, instruction, RAM input or register-bank location. A timing-resistant xtime implementation alone does not establish these fault controls.
N≈16 is the authors' expectation under reliable per-byte MSB observations, not a measured physical acquisition rate or success probability.

time.note: No numerical complete-attack offline runtime is reported.

data.note: N chosen inputs and attempted faults for one key byte. N≈16 is an author expectation; the N=20 timing result belongs to a cited earlier paper, not this fault endpoint.

memory.note: This is the table's logical shape, not a numerical peak-memory or byte-storage claim.

preprocessing.note: The source specifies this reusable table but gives no preprocessing-time measurement or normalized operation count.

success.description: Derived deterministic one-byte recovery guarantee under the existing ideal implementation-specific fault effect, localization and reliable correctness feedback. Section5.1 Eq4 fixes T[k,i]=MSB(S(k XOR i)) and selects i=0,...,N-1. Independently extract the literal standard S-box from FIPS197-upd1 Table4: all256 signatures on exactly the16 specified inputs i=0,...,15 are distinct, with minimum Hamming distance2 over all32640 pairs. Thus those16 clean observations identify every byte value, without a random-key distribution or candidate-ranking assumption. This endpoint recovers only its one initial key byte; no long-key completion is asserted. The source fault realization reveals the specified MSB with ordinary feedback polarity. This is a new finite-table deduction, not an author-printed success rate or a transfer of the N256 guarantee. The source approximately16/256 cost qualifiers, unknown time/setup/memory and original assumptions remain unchanged. Success1 is conditional on the ideal fault/feedback model; it is not measured physical acquisition yield and does not price reference encryptions or calibration.

review.scope: Independently source-first and endpoint reviewed exact finite injectivity certificate, original fault predicate, complete recovery target and native attempt count. Ideal-model guarantee only; original author estimates, resources and full-audit gates preserved.

components.description: Sections5.1–5.5: provided the specified fault effect/location and reliable correctness feedback, the target S-box output MSB is determined exactly. The specified MUL skip or input-MSB reset causes an incorrect output iff MSB1. This local observation is not physical fault acquisition or whole-key success.
